title: Regularity with separable residue field characterizes smoothness over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $S$ be a finite type $k$-algebra ($S\cong k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/\mathfrak a$ as $k$-algebras), and let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal. Let $S_{\mathfrak q}$ be the localization of $S$ at $S\setminus\mathfrak q$ and let $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$ be its residue field [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], regarded as a field extension of $k$ through $k\to S\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-pc-field-extension]. If $\kappa(\mathfrak q)/k$ is separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension], then $k\to S$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal] if and only if $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme].

proof.text: (Setup.) Write $R=S_{\mathfrak q}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$ its maximal ideal and $\kappa=\kappa(\mathfrak q)=R/\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. A field is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], so $S$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], and $R$, a localization of $S$, is a Noetherian local ring by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]; it is a $k$-algebra via $k\to S\to R$. The field $\kappa$ is generated over $k$ by the images $\bar x_1,\dots,\bar x_n$ of the generators of $S$: every element of $\kappa$ is the class of $s/t$ with $s\in S$, $t\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$, i.e. $\bar s\,\bar t^{-1}$ with $\bar s,\bar t$ polynomials over $k$ in the $\bar x_i$. So $\kappa/k$ is a finitely generated field extension, separable by hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TV (lemma-separable-smooth, lines 38754-38778)

proof.text: (The short exact sequence.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] to $A=k$, $B=R$, $\mathfrak a=\mathfrak m$, $C=R/\mathfrak m=\kappa$: the sequence $$\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\xrightarrow{\delta}\kappa\otimes_R\Omega_{R/k}\xrightarrow{w}\Omega_{\kappa/k}\to0,\qquad\delta(a\bmod\mathfrak m^2)=1\otimes\mathrm da,$$ is exact. By step 1, $R$ is a Noetherian local $k$-algebra whose residue field $\kappa$ is finitely generated and separable over $k$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-separable-residue-cotangent-injective] the map $\delta$ (which is the map $a\bmod\mathfrak m^2\mapsto\mathrm da\otimes1$ of that lemma) is injective. Hence $0\to\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\to\Omega_{R/k}\otimes_R\kappa\to\Omega_{\kappa/k}\to0$ is a short exact sequence of $\kappa$-vector spaces.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TV, lines 38754-38763 (citing Lemma 00TU lemma-computation-differential and Lemma 00RU lemma-differential-seq)

proof.text: (Dimensions.) By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] for the Noetherian local ring $R$, $e:=\dim_\kappa\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ is finite and $\dim R\le e$, with equality if and only if $R$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. By [lem-weil-pbc-separably-generated-differentials-dimension] for the finitely generated separable extension $\kappa/k$ (step 1), $\Omega_{\kappa/k}$ is finite dimensional of dimension $t:=\operatorname{trdeg}_k(\kappa)$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. A short exact sequence of vector spaces with finite-dimensional outer terms has finite-dimensional middle term of dimension the sum, so by step 2 $$\dim_\kappa\Omega_{R/k}\otimes_R\kappa=e+t.$$

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TV, lines 38764-38772

proof.text: (Passing from $R$ to $S$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] for $k\to S$ and the multiplicative set $S\setminus\mathfrak q$, the map $(\Omega_{S/k})_{\mathfrak q}\to\Omega_{R/k}$, $\mathrm ds/u\mapsto(1/u)\mathrm d(s/1)$, is an isomorphism of $R$-modules ($(\cdot)_{\mathfrak q}$ the localization of modules [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]). Tensoring with $\kappa$ over $R$: $\Omega_{R/k}\otimes_R\kappa\cong(\Omega_{S/k})_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_R\kappa\cong(\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_SR)\otimes_R\kappa\cong\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_S\kappa$, using $M_{\mathfrak q}=M\otimes_SS_{\mathfrak q}$ and associativity of the tensor product. Hence by step 3 $$\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak q)=e+t.$$

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TV, lines 38763-38764 (citing Lemma 00RT lemma-differentials-localize)

proof.text: (The comparison.) By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-local-ring-trdeg] for the finite type $k$-algebra $S$ and the prime $\mathfrak q$, $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] is finite and equals $\dim R+t$. With step 4, $$\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak q)-\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)=e-\dim R\ge0,$$ and by step 3 this difference is $0$ if and only if $R=S_{\mathfrak q}$ is a regular local ring.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TV, lines 38766-38777 (citing Lemma 00P1 lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-field)

proof.text: (Regular implies smooth.) Assume $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is a regular local ring. By step 5, $\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak q)=\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)$, in particular $\le$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-differentials-dimension-bound-smooth-at-prime] $k\to S$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TV, line 38778 ('we win by applying Lemma 00TT'), implication (2) => (1) of 00TT

proof.text: (Smooth implies regular.) Assume $k\to S$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-dimension-differentials], $\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak q)=\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)$. By step 5 the difference $e-\dim R$ is $0$, so $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme].
